text:
maria-g: heads up — seeing a cascading latency spike in us-west yesterday around 18:12 UTC. root cause points to HBM/KV-cache evictions on a handful of shared GPUs, looks like one tenant's heavy attention-heavy workloads caused repeated slab churn and pushed other tenants into tail latency.

kevin-b: ack. any p99 numbers? and which pools?

maria-g: p99 token latency jumped from ~45ms to 320ms for ~4 mins. affected pools: west-3a shared-gpu-shelf-7 and micro-silo-2. eviction rate for KVCACHE entries spiked x20. logs attached below (trimmed):
```
2026-03-22T18:12:02Z host-7: kvcache: evict slab0 tenant=acme-ai entries=1248 reason=pressure
2026-03-22T18:12:03Z host-7: hbm: alloc_fail tenant=acme-ai size=8MB
2026-03-22T18:12:05Z host-9: kvcache: evict slab1 tenant=beta-app entries=842 reason=peer-pressure
```

samir: is this noisy-tenant (acme-ai) pinned to dedicated? sounds like shared

maria-g: not dedicated. they run large attention windows and a lot of parallel streams. their KV reuse pattern is poor; keeps thrashing. we saw similar earlier but lower severity.

olivia-s: can we do per-tenant kvcache quotas or TTLs? that would stop one tenant from blowing out slabs.

kevin-b: per-tenant quotas make sense, but we'd have to roll a config change across runtime. risk of regressing throughput for small tenants. alternative — steer acme-ai to a burst lane / dedicated micro-slice while we triage.

samir: steering would reduce interference fast. question: do we have capacity for a micro-slice in west-3a without breaking SLA for dedicated customers?

maria-g: we have 2 warm ephemeral GPUs in west-3a but they are used for canaries. capacity looks tight. long-term: slab-tagging to reserve 20% of KVCACHE per tenant for fairness. short-term: routing tweak + soft-quota to slow acme-ai clients.

kevin-b: can we implement soft-quota as a router-level backpressure — throttle token-rate when tenant kvcache evict rate > threshold? minimal runtime changes.

maria-g: yes that's doable. simple heuristic: if eviction_rate > 100/s for 60s -> route to burst lane OR add per-request delay token-bucket of 50rps. fallback to dedicated if they request.

olivia-s: adding a soft backpressure also reduces cost — prevents noisy tenant from causing others to spin more tokens and raise unit cost.

samir: assignable? i can prototype router throttle today and run in canary for west-3a.

kevin-b: cool. samir, please also add a metric for "kvcache_throttle_count" and an alert if we throttle > 5% of tenant traffic for > 5m.

samir: noted. will push canary config under exp/routing/throttle/acme-ai by EOD and post rollout results.

infra-bot: deploy-bot started canary: exp/routing/throttle/acme-ai -> west-3a (canary). build: 0.9.7

maria-g: one more ask — let's schedule a follow-up next week to discuss slab-tagging design and cost tradeoffs. tagging implies reserving memory slices which could reduce overall utilization.

kevin-b: agreed. calendar invite: "HBM slab-tagging + soft-quota tradeoffs". matt/policy team should join.

olivia-s: also include cost model: reserved vs observed tail cost increase. I can pull numbers once canary runs.

maria-g: thanks team. samir — ping here with canary metrics (eviction rate, p99, throttle count) after 1h and after 24h.

samir: will do. :rocket:
